But note: for energies below 0.1 MeV, we don't have data; but for scattered photons, energy can be lower than 0.1 MeV. The Klein-Nishina distribution can produce scattered photon energies as low as 0.2 MeV? At 2 MeV, the minimum scattered photon energy is at 180° scattering: E' = E / (1 + 2α) = 2 / (1 + 2*2/0.511) = 2 / (1 + 7.826) = 2/8.826 = 0.2266 MeV. So scattered photon energy is >0.226 MeV for primary 2 MeV. For multiple scattering, energies can be lower. But for first scatter, minimum is 0.227 MeV. So energies down to 0.1 MeV may be rare but possible from multiple scatter. We'll assume cross sections are valid down to 0.01 MeV maybe using extrapolation. Our functions will extrapolate constant beyond the range; that may be inaccurate but okay for a few events.
